title: A dry runs import reports would-import for a run the door would refuse
body:
## Summary
importRuns' dry mode (the CLI default) only runs skipOf, so a run whose Run door or option read refuses it is reported `would-import` and turns `refused` only under --yes.

## Description
lib/import/runs.ts:116 `if (opts.dry) { out.push({... outcome: 'would-import' }) }` never calls land(): readRunIn (records/launch.ts) and parseAt('imported run', runSchema) (runs.ts:75) run only on the wet pass. The CLI's dry report (pipeline/import/runs.mts) is what the operator reads before --yes, so its count is the count the wet run may not meet. tests/next-server/import-runs.test.ts:107 even pins `imported === would-import` over the fixture universe, which holds only because no fixture is refused. Fixed: dry runs land() inside a transaction that always rolls back (throw a DRY sentinel; store.tx returns its err and ROLLBACKs), reporting `would-import` or `refused` with the door's sentence.

## Flow
- build a V1Run whose input the run door refuses (an extract slug outside its regex reaches the door through readRunIn)
- importRuns(s, [run], {dry:true}) -> would-import
- importRuns(s, [run], {dry:false}) -> refused
- after: dry -> refused with the same reason, nothing written

## Expected impact
The dry report becomes the wet run's promise. Could break: a dry run takes BEGIN IMMEDIATE (the write lock) for each run - on the operator's store, under a live worker, that is lock contention a read never caused; the worker must measure busy time.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a dry run's outcomes are the wet run's
Before: dry evaluates 1 of the 3 refusal sources (skipOf; not readRunIn, not the run door) - read from runs.ts:61-101
After: 3 of 3 (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked runs.ts; the instrument (a refused V1Run fixture) is S but the fix takes a write lock in a dry mode, M risk 4, not landed unread
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
lib/import/runs.ts:116-119 (dry branch never calls land)
lib/import/runs.ts:71 readRunIn, :75 parseAt(runSchema), :86 throw rec.error - wet only
instrument: a V1Run the run door refuses, run dry and wet through importRuns on a temp store; Before dry=would-import / wet=refused, After both refused; plus busy-ms of a dry pass beside a held write tx

title: The import preview never runs the creation door, so a project compose refuses is promised as import
body:
## Summary
stageProject grades a project `import` without calling compose's door; compose runs only inside commit's land(), so any input the door refuses (units it will not plan, a runtime it will not take) is a preview that says import and a commit that says refused.

## Description
lib/import/project.ts:159-164 derives units from v1's targetS through filmDefaults with no bound; probed this round: filmDefaults(1e9) plans prompts 16,666,667 and filmDefaults(1e300) plans prompts 1.67e298 (plates and shots cap at 200/67). The values reach compose at lib/import/commit.ts:139 and putProject's runtimeS at :142; whatever the compose/units schema refuses is discovered there, after the operator confirmed a preview that said `import`. The golden path (import-normalization, review-before-commit): the review shows what the commit will do. Fixed: stage the compose input through composeInputSchema (the door compose parses first, packages/kernel/src/records/write.ts:65) at staging and refuse there with its sentence; bound targetS to the template's range.

## Flow
- v1 project row with targetS 1e9
- planImport -> outcome import
- commitImport -> outcome refused (or a project with 16.7M prompts, if the door takes it)
- after: refused at the preview with the door's sentence

## Expected impact
A damaged v1 row is refused before the operator confirms, by name. Could break: a v1 project whose targetS the door refuses today but nobody noticed would now be refused at preview - the same outcome, earlier.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the preview's outcome is the commit's
Before: filmDefaults(1e9).prompts = 16,666,667; filmDefaults(1e300).prompts = 1.67e298 (probe, vitest scratch file, this round); doors run at staging for the project row: 0 of 1
After: 1 of 1 (predicted)
Method: simulation - the units figure is a probe; what compose then does with it was not run (no temp-store compose of a 1e9 target this round)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
probe: filmDefaults(90)=18/6/2, (1e5)=200/67/1667, (1e9)=200/67/16666667, (1e300)=200/67/1.67e298
lib/import/project.ts:159 targetS unbounded
lib/import/commit.ts:139 compose only at commit
instrument: import-roundtrip case: putProject({...seed.film, targetS: 1e9}); preview outcome vs commit outcome on a temp universe

title: Staging scans every step, asset and upload once per project and per asset
body:
## Summary
planImport filters the archive's whole steps and assets lists once per project, and bytesOf finds an upload by a linear scan once per asset: O(projects x steps + projects x assets + assets x uploads), run twice per import (preview, then the confirm re-stages).

## Description
lib/import/project.ts:132 `archive.rows.steps.filter((s) => s['projectId'] === v1Id)`, :137 themes.find, :144 assets.filter, and the `strings` walk over every row; lib/import/shelf.ts:153 `archive.rows.uploads.find((x) => x['id'] === up)` per asset; commit.ts:250 planImport again at confirm. An account of dozens of projects is milliseconds; the archive cap allows 250,000 lines (archive.ts ARCHIVE_CAPS), where the products reach ~1e10 comparisons. Fixed: index steps by projectId and uploads/themes/assets by id once per archive (Maps built in planImport).

## Flow
- synthesize an archive at the line cap: 1,000 projects x 100 steps, 20,000 assets x 1 upload
- time planImport on a temp store
- after: the same with Maps

## Expected impact
A large account previews in bounded time. Could break: nothing semantic - the lookups return the same rows; insertion order must be kept for steps (v1's key order).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - staging time on a large archive
Before: not measured (no synthetic large archive built this round)
After: not measured
Method: simulation - complexity read from project.ts/shelf.ts; the timing harness is S but was not built
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
lib/import/project.ts:132,137,144 per-project scans
lib/import/shelf.ts:153 per-asset uploads.find
lib/import/commit.ts:250 re-stage at confirm
instrument: a vitest timing case over writeArchive-built synthetic archive (1k projects x 100 steps, 20k assets) - planImport ms before/after

title: The runs importer checks each v1 run against every job by an unindexed json_extract
body:
## Summary
skipOf runs `SELECT 1 FROM jobs WHERE json_extract(record, '$.of.id') = ?` once per v1 run; jobs has no index on of.id, so each check scans the whole jobs table.

## Description
lib/import/runs.ts:65; packages/kernel/src/job.ts:47-68 indexes jobs on lane/state/ord only. A runs import over R v1 runs against a store of J jobs is R full scans with a JSON parse per row. One-time CLI (pipeline/import/runs.mts), dry by default and run again with --yes, so twice. Fixed: one read per importRuns call building the Set of of.id values (or check the run's own job id runJobId(runId) by primary key first and fall back to the scan only for an of.id the id rule does not cover).

## Flow
- seed a temp store with 5,000 jobs
- importRuns dry over 500 V1Runs
- time it; after: the Set read

## Expected impact
The operator's one-time import finishes in one scan instead of R. Could break: a job created between the Set read and a run's tx is missed by the dry check - land's insertRun would then hit its conflict and report refused, as a race does today.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - importRuns time on a populated store
Before: not measured
After: not measured
Method: simulation - no populated store built this round
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
lib/import/runs.ts:65 json_extract per run
packages/kernel/src/job.ts:47,48,68 (no of.id index)
instrument: vitest timing case: temp kernel with 5k recordImportedJobIn jobs, importRuns dry over 500 runs, ms before/after

title: A kernel rename of an imported project is lost on re-export, and nothing says so
body:
## Summary
exportProjects writes an imported project's row as the ORIGINAL v1 row from the import record, so a title or runtime changed in the kernel since the import goes back to v1 as it was before, while export.ts's header discloses the down-conversion only for step records.

## Description
lib/import/export.ts:138 `into.projects.push(await restored(rec.value.project))` - the kernel project (loadProject, export.ts:63) is read for recipe/title/runtimeS but only the composed-project road (v1ProjectOf, :96) uses them. The header (:19-32) promises an exact round trip for every record nobody edited and v1's shape for an edited one; the project row has neither rule. registry import-normalization/lossy-conversion-disclosure: a lossy export says what it loses. Fixed: overlay the kernel's title and runtimeS (as targetS) on the restored row when they differ from the original's, or name the loss in the export's answer.

## Flow
- import the seeded film
- rename it in the kernel (putProject title)
- exportProjects -> projects row title is v1's old title

## Expected impact
The operator's rename survives the trip back to v1. Could break: the byte-exact re-export of an unedited project row must stay byte-exact - overlay only on a difference.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - kernel edits to an imported project's row reach the re-export
Before: fields of the kernel project row the re-export carries for an imported project: 0 of 2 (title, runtimeS) - read from export.ts:421
After: 2 of 2 (predicted)
Method: simulation - read the export path; the rename-then-export case is S but changes the wire rows v1 reads (in-tree reader lib/studioArchive.ts), so a contract card
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence:
lib/import/export.ts:138 restored original project row
lib/import/export.ts:96-113 v1ProjectOf uses title/runtimeS (composed road only)
instrument: import-roundtrip case: import, rename in kernel, export; assert title; plus the existing byte-exact case stays green (verifier: inspectArchive)
